articles.title: 有图有真相：姜超谈红魔 12 Pro+ 和 iPhone Duo 屏下前摄实际表现差异，称差距应该是显而易见的
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，红魔游戏手机产品总经理姜超刚刚发文，谈及了红魔和 iPhone Duo 的屏下前摄实际表现差异。他表示，有图有真相，差距应该是显而易见的：红魔 12 Pro+ 的屏下隐藏效果，已经很难察觉前摄的存在；而 iPhone Duo 的屏下区域，仍能明显看到一个半透明的小孔。单就隐藏效果来看，观感大概相当于第二代屏下的水平，而红魔 12 Pro+ 已经进化到了第九代。想把这个“孔”真正藏好，确实不容易。我们花了五六年的时间，一代代摸索、迭代，才逐步做到今天这个效果。当然，一块好屏幕，不只是把前摄藏起来。分辨率、帧率、边框，我们同样一直在打磨。红魔 12 Pro+ 不仅做到了目前行业最高的 185Hz 刷新率，还把边框收窄到了 0.96mm。技术没有捷径。这块更完整、更纯粹的屏幕，就是我们一代代死磕出来的答案。IT之家附红魔游戏手机产品总经理姜超实拍对比图如下：

articles.title: 上市满三个月，长鑫科技正式被纳入上证指数位列第一大权重股
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，根据中证指数公司网站最新披露数据，长鑫科技已被纳入上证综合指数，权重为 4.67%，位列第一大权重股。农业银行、工商银行紧随其后，权重分别为 3.83% 和 3.77%。与长鑫科技于 2026 年 7 月 27 日登陆科创板，至 10 月 27 日正好满三个月。根据上证综合指数编制方案，上市以来日均总市值排名沪市前 10 位的证券，在上市满三个月后计入指数。长鑫科技上市后总市值一度突破 3 万亿元，长期位居 A 股总市值前列，满足上述计入条件。同日，长鑫科技也被纳入上证科创板综合指数，权重高达 15.74%，同样位列第一大权重股，寒武纪、海光信息在该指数中分列二、三位。两个指数合计来看，长鑫科技在上证综指中以 4.67% 的权重居首，在科创综指中更以接近 16% 的占比占据绝对主导地位。此次调整发生在规则变化之后不久。10 月 26 日，上海证券交易所与中证指数有限公司修订的上证系列综合指数编制方案正式实施，新增了单个样本权重不超过 15% 的上限规则。长鑫科技在科创综指的权重恰好触及这一上限附近，而在上证综指的权重远低于红线。IT之家注意到，根据编制方案，权重因子常规于每月第二个星期五的下一交易日调整，新计入样本权重超过 15% 时也会触发额外调整。市场层面，纳入消息公布前后，长鑫科技股价表现活跃。10 月 28 日盘中，该股涨幅一度超过 4%，近四个交易日累计涨幅超过 12%。存储芯片板块的整体反弹为股价提供了支撑，而指数纳入带来的被动资金配置预期，也被市场视为短期催化因素之一。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，Ubiquiti 当地时间 10 月 26 日宣布推出 UniFi 长距离交换机。该设备搭配兼容的户外长距离终端可将 PoE 供电延伸到 800m 的距离，简化户外网络部署。该网络交换机提供 8 个支持 PoE+++ 的 100MbE RJ-45、1 个 1GbE RJ-45、1 个 1GbE SFP，集成 1.3W 触控屏。其总 PoE 功率达 630W，单端口 PoE 输出功率可达 90W，在 100m 上可提供 71.3W、在 800m 上可提供 13W。Ubiquiti UniFi Long-Range Switch 8 PoE 交换机本体售价 249 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,664 元人民币），每个户外长距离终端则是 99 美元（现汇率约合 661.4 元人民币）。

articles.title: 黑客连环攻击韩国金融业：多家虚拟货币交易所、券商遭入侵
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，韩联社今日报道称，据韩国金融部门和有关行业今日消息，虚拟货币交易所“Bithumb”、未来资产环球投资和大信证券三家单位遭到了黑客攻击。大和证券今日表示，3.849 万名客户的个人信息和信用信息遭到泄露。Bithumb 前一天发现，公司内部移动办公系统遭外部未授权人员异常访问，导致个人信息泄露，公司正对会员信息等具体泄露范围进行分析。金融监督院已向大信证券派出现场调查组，进一步了解情况。IT之家从原报道获悉，继未来资产人寿保险公司本月 26 日发生系统入侵事件导致客户信息泄露后，Bithumb、未来资产环球投资、大信证券也被发现遭遇黑客攻击。至此，除了信用卡公司外，韩国主要金融行业几乎均已确认遭受黑客攻击的情况。相关阅读：《韩国多家银行遭黑客攻击致个人信息泄露，总统李在明下令彻查》《韩国五大商业银行首次同时被黑客攻击，其中三家发生客户信息泄露》《韩国外交系统遭遇黑客攻击，致现任与前任雇员个人信息泄露》《韩国警方闹乌龙：数百万美元比特币在眼皮底下被盗，恢复密钥竟被拱手送给第三方黑客》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，Windows 11 系统目前兼容原生运行的最古老图形 GUI 应用是谁？可以追溯到几年前？科技博客 enlyth 于 10 月 26 日发布博文，带着这个问题，探究背后的答案。该博主通过测试，认为一款链接日期为 1992 年 11 月 16 日的 Windows 图形界面程序 CDPLAYER.EXE，无需修改、无需模拟器，即可在最新版 Windows 11 上启动，并可通过虚拟光驱播放音频。IT之家附上相关图片如下：1992 年 11 月 16 日的 Windows 图形界面程序 CDPLAYER.EXE若以发布时间计算，这款程序至今已接近 34 年，被认为可能是目前仍能在 Windows 11 上原生运行的最古老 GUI 应用。该程序源自 Windows NT 3.1 的早期预发布版本 Build 347。博主在翻查互联网档案馆中的旧系统镜像时发现，同期多数程序因可执行文件格式、Windows API 调用约定或捆绑 C 运行库不兼容而崩溃；但 CDPLAYER.EXE 改用系统自带的 crtdll.dll，而 Windows 11 的 32 位兼容目录中仍保留该动态链接库，因此得以继续运行。由于现代电脑普遍没有 CD-ROM 光驱，直接启动时会提示找不到光驱。测试者借助一个小型 DLL 模拟光驱并注入虚拟音频数据后，这款老程序成功播放音频，界面和基本功能仍可使用。博主此前发现修改日期为 1993 年 2 月 22 日的《空当接龙》FREECELL.EXE 也能在 Windows 11 上完整运行，当时认为这已是“最古老”答案。此次发现的 1992 年 CD 播放器，把纪录又提前了约 3 个月。1993 年 2 月 22 日的 FREECELL.EXE 可以在 Windows 11 上运行，已有 33 年零 8 个月的历史需要说明的是，这一纪录限定为“原生运行、不修改、不使用模拟器”。若借助 otvdm 等兼容层，取自 Windows 1.01、日期为 1985 年 11 月 15 日的黑白棋游戏 REVERSI.EXE 也能在 Windows 11 上游玩。REVERSI.EXE

articles.title: 斯特兰蒂斯 2026 财年第三季度归母净亏损 4.7 亿欧元，同比收窄约 90%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，斯特兰蒂斯今日发布 2026 财年（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 12 月）前三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）及第三财季（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告：2026 财年前三季度营业总收入：1192.25 亿欧元，同比增长 7%归母净利润：1.86 亿欧元，同比扭亏为盈经营现金流：-68.17 亿欧元，净流出同比收窄 0.3%自由现金流：-49.3 亿欧元，同比增长 33%稀释每股收益：0.02 欧元2026 财年第三财季营业总收入：376.11 亿欧元，同比增长 1%归母净利润：-4.7 亿欧元，同比收窄约 89.65%经营现金流：-39.3 亿欧元，同比收窄约 14%自由现金流：-40.09 亿欧元，同比增长 7%稀释每股收益：-0.18 欧元 AI 解读斯泰兰蒂斯 2026 年前三季度业绩显著修复，净营收同比增长 1% 至 1192.25 亿欧元，归母净利润由去年同期大额亏损转为盈利 1.86 亿欧元，工业自由现金流同比改善 33%，收窄至 49.3 亿欧元。公司主营业务与本季亮点斯泰兰蒂斯是一家全球性汽车集团，旗下拥有 Abarth、Alfa Romeo、Chrysler、Citroën、DS Automobiles、FIAT、Jeep、Lancia、Maserati、Opel、Peugeot、Ram、Vauxhall、Free2move、Leasys 等品牌。本次同时披露了 2026 财年三财季（单季度）与前三季度累计（YTD）两套数据，核心亮点如下：2026 财年三财季（单季度）：净营收 376.11 亿欧元，同比增长 1%；经调整营业利润 2.56 亿欧元，同比增长 184%，利润率为 0.7%，同比提高 0.5 个百分点；归母净亏损 4.70 亿欧元，同比收窄约 90%；工业自由现金流净流出 40.09 亿欧元，同比收窄约 7%。2026 财年前三季度（YTD）：净营收 1192.25 亿欧元，同比增长 7%；经调整营业利润 19.89 亿欧元，同比增长 216%；归母净利润 1.86 亿欧元，同比扭亏为盈；工业自由现金流净流出 49.30 亿欧元，同比收窄 33%。区域经营表现北美：三财季净营收 155.86 亿欧元，同比下降 3%，AOI 由亏转盈至 6400 万欧元；市场份额升至 7.5%，Ram 品牌北美销量同比增长 30%。扩大欧洲：三财季净营收 140.62 亿欧元，同比增长 3%，但 AOI 亏损 3.11 亿欧元；EU30 销量同比增长 1%，纯电销量同比增长 65%。南美：三财季净营收 41.2 亿欧元，同比增长 3%，AOI 4.31 亿欧元；在巴西、阿根廷保持区域第一。中东及非洲：三财季净营收 16.73 亿欧元，同比下降 19%，AOI 2.44 亿欧元，AOI 利润率 14.6%，同比提升 140 个基点。亚太：三财季净营收 4.45 亿欧元，同比下降 7%，AOI 由亏转盈至 1800 万欧元，AOI 利润率同比改善 480 个基点。2026 全年指引与展望公司重申 2026 年财务指引：净营收实现中个位数百分比增长；AOI 利润率维持低个位数百分比；工业自由现金流同比改善（含 2025 下半年相关约 16 亿欧元的现金支付），并预计 2027 年实现工业自由现金流转正。CEO 表示价值创造计划（VCP）已在本季贡献正向收益，预计到年底完成 40% 的总年化效率目标，第四季度 VCP 节省金额预计为第三季度的约两倍。流动性与投资价值截止 2026 年 9 月 30 日，工业可用流动性为 426.52 亿欧元，占过去 12 个月净营收的 26%，处于公司 25%-30% 目标区间内，资产负债表稳健。当前业绩处于 FaSTLAne 2030 转型早期修复阶段，盈利与现金流改善趋势明确，但欧洲业务仍承压，投资者可关注后续 VCP 落地节奏及 2027 年现金流转正的兑现情况。风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: 近乎垂直拉升：AI 成放大器，2026 年漏洞报告数量“爆表”
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息，科技媒体 gigazine 今天（10 月 28 日）发布博文，报道称开发者 @0x_Osprey 制作了网页 CVE Tracker，通过可视化图表追踪已获得 CVE（通用漏洞标识符）编号的漏洞数量变化，清晰呈现出 2026 年以来漏洞报告数量的陡峭上升曲线。IT之家注：CVE 是全球广泛使用的漏洞编号体系，通常被安全研究者、软件厂商和企业用于追踪、修复与通报安全缺陷。CVE Tracker 将这些公开记录整理为趋势图，用户还可查看主流 AI 模型的发布时间，从而观察其与漏洞发现高峰之间的关联。IT之家注：该网站只有深色方案报道指出，AI 公司往往会在模型正式发布前，就使用测试版本开展漏洞挖掘和报告，因此模型上线时间未必与漏洞数量激增完全同步。该媒体称 AI 正在成为安全研究的“放大器”，能更快速地扫描代码、复现异常行为、整理报告，从而让人力难以覆盖的软件角落也被纳入检查范围。但漏洞“被发现得更多”，并不必然意味着系统“变得更危险”。更多报告既可能暴露真实风险，也可能带来低质量、重复或难以验证的漏洞报告，进而加重开源维护者和安全团队的分诊压力。

articles.title: 美国一公司招人遛机器狗：时薪 20 美元，不用铲屎但可能要扛狗回来
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 28 日消息据《纽约时报》报道，，本月早些时候，旧金山一家初创公司发布了一则奇特的招聘启事：招募人员遛机器狗，无需相关经验。遛机器狗的时薪和遛真狗大致相当，但机器狗需要在城市人行道上转悠更久来完成采集任务。招聘广告写明，每次要连续步行四到六个小时。好的是，你不用收拾它的排泄物。不好的是，机器狗和真狗一样会耍脾气。就像普通狗狗可能突然趴在繁忙马路中间不肯挪步，机器狗也可能中途罢工 —— 原因是设备过热。遛狗员这时得把这台四足机械抱回初创公司办公室。广告特意提醒应聘者，必须能够稳妥搬动大约 33 磅（约 15 公斤）重的设备。这份现已删除的招聘帖给出的时薪为 20 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 133.6 元人民币），由名叫 Dimensional 的初创公司发布在脸书群组“湾区工作”里。有意思的是，公司所在地正是旧金山一个名为狗斑（Dogpatch）的街区。帖子下面只有寥寥几条评论，没有人觉得这件事很怪异。一位母亲留言：“我儿子感兴趣，可以立刻上岗。”Dimensional 创始人斯塔什 · 波米希特（Stash Pomichter）称，公司正在开发一套面向机器人的开源操作系统。26 岁的波米希特希望把智能体嵌入机器人，让用户可以指挥它们在现实世界干活。波米希特坚信，人们理应可以指挥机器人搬运重箱子、运送物品。他在采访中说：“人类还在干这类体力活，说实话，这实在太原始了。”不过，在机器狗帮我们拎杂货、替我们干重活之前，Dimensional 先要提升机器人在城市环境里自主导航的能力。这就是招募遛机器狗员的原因：工作人员操控、引导机器狗，同时它搭载的摄像头与传感器记录行进过程，生成波米希特所说的“真实基准数据”。有当地居民拍到有人牵着这台四足机器狗，还把视频发给了《纽约时报》，他感慨旧金山本身就很古怪，现在变得愈发离谱。Dimensional 并不是硬件厂商。波米希特介绍，公司已经从美国、中国、德国的厂商采购了 100 多台机器狗和 50 台人形机器人，自研可以对接 AI 智能体的操作系统，让机器拥有更强自主能力。本月交给遛狗员、价值 2,000 美元（现汇率约合 13,362 元人民币）的机器狗来自中国宇树科技（Unitree），出厂即可通过遥控器或者手机 App 操控。Dimensional 对比了两种模式下机器狗的表现：人工操控，以及由 AI 智能体自主控制。结果发现 AI 智能体的控制能力还差很多。“从这次遛狗实验我们得出结论：AI 智能体控制硬件的能力仍然很差，”波米希特说，“现阶段依旧需要人类参与其中。”他们的目标是让机器人投入工厂、数据中心、建筑工地，或是担任安保巡逻。类似的应用已经落地：亚特兰大一处公寓小区就有机器狗巡逻，远在菲律宾的工作人员远程值守。这台机器本质上就是一台可移动的安防摄像头，供远端人员查看画面。波米希特说，他给一台机器狗写好了程序，让它夜间在仓库式的公司办公室巡逻。他给它的提示词是“你是全世界最优秀的安保犬”，要求它跟踪午夜之后进入大楼的任何人。一旦侦测到人，机器狗就给他发短信，他再调取监控，判断来人是加班的员工还是闯入者。并不是所有人都对在狗斑街区游荡的机器狗抱以玩味的态度。Dimensional 想给 AI 智能体赋予实体躯体，而当下越来越多人担心，更强大的 AI 或许会对人类造成威胁。这种类似《终结者》的联想，让一名男子十分警惕。他去到公司办公地点，随后给 Dimensional 员工发送充满威胁的短信，声称这些机器狗会被改造成武器。《纽约时报》看到了这条消息：“等着帮着随便屠杀普通人吧，败类。”Dimensional 已经向警方报案。“以后我们可能会遇到更多这类情况，”波米希特说，“如果真是这样，那我们或许需要更多巡逻机器狗。”

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.35942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. I contrast a stopwatch view, on which time saved is whatever the clock records, with a ledger view, on which it is a counterfactual that has to be read next to the errors the work lets through, and I argue for the latter. The argument has four parts. I define a model-free pair of quantities, time saved and excess escaped defects, and one decision number built from them: the break-even defect cost. I give a baseline model of checking in which, until the model is good enough not to check, a calibrated worker's escaped-defect rate does not depend on how good the model is; checking time grows with the logarithm of the model's error rate; and over-trust buys minutes on the clock at a larger cost in total minutes. Abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. articles.title: Why and How to Do Science When AI Is Better at It: A Framework Grounded in Human Understanding and Direction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36116v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI begins to match or exceed human researchers at core scientific tasks, two questions become pressing: \emph{why} should humans keep doing science, and \emph{how} should they use AI when they do? This paper argues that the second can be answered only by answering the first. It holds that one indispensable aim of science is \emph{durable, collective human understanding of the world, pursued in service of human ends and values}. From this principle it derives a two-part test for when a research task can be delegated to AI. The first part, \emph{human understanding}, requires that the scientific community remain able to explain, defend and contest the resulting claims, and retain the skills to do so. The second, \emph{human direction}, requires that judgments about which questions matter and what findings mean stay with accountable humans. Abstract: Prompt optimization should improve the image a user receives without changing the scene the user requested. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36169v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A retrieval-augmented language model answers from two sources, the retrieved context and its own knowledge, and the two disagree whenever the context is incomplete or wrong. Existing methods settle the disagreement with a rule fixed at design time: follow the context, amplify it in proportion to how far it moves the model, or trust the model's memory. Each rule is confidently wrong in some deployment. In a decision-theoretic model of two sources, the score of any fixed rule is linear in the share of reliable contexts while the best attainable score is convex, so every fixed rule is beaten wherever it is not exactly optimal; and a symmetric divergence between the two sources, the signal adaptive decoding uses, carries no information about which one is right. Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on reusable skills for complex software engineering tasks, making skill libraries essential for repository development and maintenance. Abstract: Sequential recommendation models typically predict a user's next action from recent session interactions, which limits personalization when short-term signals are weak or ambiguous. Abstract: Machine learning models deployed behind query interfaces expose more than their predictions, because an adversary can use those predictions to rebuild the model itself. Model stealing attacks (MSAs) exploit this exposure by training a surrogate model that replicates the decision behavior of a target through black-box queries alone, without access to its parameters or training data. SNNs communicate through sparse, discrete spikes, and their outputs depend on membrane potentials that evolve over time rather than on a static mapping from input to output. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36335v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well across many real-world tasks but remain prone to hallucination, limiting their reliability in domains such as biomedicine and healthcare, where answers must be grounded in established knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this problem by incorporating external information, but often overlooks logical relationships and relies heavily on the LLM's own reasoning, which can compromise answer faithfulness. We propose OA-RAG, an agent that integrates formal reasoning with LLM reasoning, drawing on both the logical structure and informal annotations of domain ontologies. For each answer, OA-RAG reports the ontology observations used as evidence and a model-assessed grounding level (entailed, supported, related, or unrelated) that characterises the strength of that evidence. Abstract: Early AI programs were often also theories of how people think, and programs that wrote programs were, in part, theories of how people program. The first, Herbert Simon's Heuristic Compiler (1961), was an experimental model of programming as problem-solving, applying the means-ends analysis methods of the General Problem Solver to investigate the nature of the programming task. Abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs), which process both visual inputs and text queries, incur high inference costs due to the large number of visual tokens, making visual token pruning a natural approach for improving efficiency. Abstract: Activation steering is a popular approach for shifting LLM output toward a desired behavior, and increasingly for generating realistic synthetic data. Abstract: Individual fairness in machine learning requires that similar individuals receive similar predictions. We study local predictive consistency as a node-level relaxation of pairwise individual fairness, where each prediction is compared with a similarity-weighted average of predictions in its local neighborhood. Abstract: Quantization, pruning, and model merging are popular transformations applied to deployment-ready LLMs to improve efficiency and downstream performance. Recent work has shown that these transformations can introduce a security threat: an adversary can train a model that passes safety checks in its pre-transformed state, only turning malicious once it is transformed for deployment. In this work, we introduce a simple, composable attack framework that targets multiple transformations simultaneously and triggers when any one of them is applied by a user. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33307v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Boruta is a widely used method for selecting gene panels from RNA sequencing data, and its most used implementation recommends Random Forest trees of depth 3 to 7, an untested setting. We tested whether this setting changes which genes are selected, using pan-cancer data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (10,469 tumors, 33 cancer types) and breast cancer PAM50 subtyping (981 tumors, 5 subtypes). A leakage-free protocol fitted every label-dependent step inside training folds, measured every effect against seed-to-seed variation, and held out a locked test set per task. In pan-cancer data, shallow trees changed the selection far more than a new seed did: the top-500 overlap with unlimited-depth selections was 0.37 at depth 5, against 0.84 to 0.93 between seeds at depth 5 or unlimited depth. Shallow trees confirmed 3.5 times fewer genes, missed markers of large classes and produced less accurate 50-gene panels (balanced accuracy 0.809 vs 0.889).

arXiv:2610.33315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.33331v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adversarial training remains one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, but its standard PGD-based training is computationally expensive because adversarial examples are generated for every training sample. Selective adversarial training reduces this cost by perturbing only a subset of samples. However, existing selective techniques typically rely on point-wise difficulty signals such as loss, entropy, margin, or gradients. We show that these point-wise criteria do not capture local instability in a sample's neighborhood. Motivated by this, we propose Augmentation-Guided Adversarial Training (AGAT), a selective adversarial training framework that uses augmentation-induced local variation to allocate samples with unstable neighborhoods for adversarial training. Abstract: Training contextual masking systems for personally identifiable information (PII) requires examples distinguishing maskable from preservable mentions of one entity type, but privacy restrictions limit access to real data. Author-based augmentation (SPY) labels mentions unrelated to the author as non-PII, presuming a single data subject and overlooking others. Abstract: System One decision models such as Jev answer structured questions in a single forward pass without generating text, offering fast and computationally efficient clinical decision support. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36083v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). Abstract: Bengali, spoken by over 230 million people, remains severely under-resourced in spoken language research. Existing open Bengali ASR corpora are confined to short, read or crowd-sourced speech and lack speaker diarization and long-form audio.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Election integrity is a shared commitment in American politics, but Democrats and Republicans in Congress increasingly mean different things by it. Analyzing 10,420 congressional e-newsletters sent from 2010 to 2025, we examine how the two parties invoke election terms such as ``integrity,'' ``security,'' and ``fraud.'' Using diachronic word embeddings, which track semantic change through how words are used in context, we measure how differently each party uses each term, how much each party shifts, and whether they share nearest semantic neighbors. We show that members of Congress do not need different words to tell different stories about elections. They need only place those same words in different company. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often answer ambiguous inputs as if they had a single intended meaning. Abstract: Homoglyph and invisible-character watermarks are edit-based watermarks. Instead of changing how a model generates text, they hide a signal in the text after it is written. Abstract: When a Large Language Model (LLM) is trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) on multiple tasks, a task's primary reward can gate auxiliary rewards such as a length reward: on a failing response, an auxiliary cannot exceed the primary. Abstract: A major challenge facing AI scientific discovery pipelines is how to determine when a generated idea is meaningfully novel. Abstract: Emergent generative AI technologies, while remarkably beneficial across several tasks and domains, can suffer from unforeseen vulnerabilities and difficult-to-anticipate failure modes. We show that when VLMs are requested to transform human face images to reflect race identities (e.g., Hispanic, Black, White, or Asian) and sexual orientation (e.g., gay or straight), VLMs often comply with such requests. We demonstrate that compliance (and refusal) is non-deterministic, group-sensitive, and generated images are statistically distinguishable, often accentuating deep-seated stereotypes. arXiv:2610.36022v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. arXiv:2610.36150v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense geometry from a set of images with a feed-forward network, but they expect pinhole images. That assumption is inside the backbone too: the positional encoding and the training loss both bind an image position to a direction in space, and both depend on the lens. We condition both on the dense ray field, the unit direction through every pixel, which describes any central camera without a lens type, distortion coefficients or a bound on field of view. Angular coordinates give the rotary encoding the measured ray angle of each patch, evaluated per view, and solid-angle weighting scales the point loss by the area each pixel covers on the sphere, so neither the encoding nor the supervision depends on the lens. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has rapidly become the preferred representation for high-fidelity novel view synthesis and 3D scene reconstruction. However, the learned representation encodes sensitive visual information including human faces, license plates, documents, and computer screens, raising significant privacy concerns when trained splats are shared or deployed. In this work, we address the underexplored problem of privacy preservation in Gaussian Splatting by proposing a representation-level anonymization framework that directly anonymizes a trained splat. Given a trained splat and a user-provided reference view identifying sensitive content, our method localizes the corresponding regions in the underlying 3D representation and directly anonymizes them, ensuring that the sensitive information is absent from all subsequently rendered novel views while preserving the overall scene geometry and visual fidelity. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36192v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning velocity fields directly in pixel space is difficult and slow. We show that coarse second-order image statistics can ease this task: frozen Wiener estimates improve velocity learning, with gains extending beyond the linear predictions they explicitly provide. Moreover, we observe similar but complementary gains from frozen bases and pixel decoding. These observations motivate Wiener-informed Decoding (WiD), which uses statistical knowledge both for direct prediction and to organize decoder computation without modifying native blocks. WiD combines a trainable Wiener prediction path with coefficient interfaces that inject features into the native decoder and return its predicted coefficient corrections, with these components initialized with data statistics. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite rapid progress in visual understanding and document transcription, modern vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with a fundamental accessibility task: reading Braille from images. We introduce BrailleBench, a manually curated benchmark of 259 real-world Grade-1 and Grade-2 Braille images. We evaluate proprietary, open-weight, OCR-specialized, and tool-assisted multimodal systems and find that standalone general-purpose models perform poorly at directly transcribing Braille images, whereas tool-assisted systems perform much better. We design a synthetic Braille generation pipeline with diverse layouts and image perturbations. A 2B VLM model trained on our synthetic data reaches 87% exact match on Grade-1 and 61% on Grade-2 BrailleBench, outperforming standalone VLMs and achieving the highest Grade-2 exact match score among the evaluated systems. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Monocular 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) remains unreliable under weak observations caused by long camera-to-person distances, occlusion, and motion blur. In challenging scenarios such as sports, these factors make the problem highly ambiguous, as different 3D poses may yield similar 2D projections. This ambiguity is especially severe for one-stage HMR, which recovers all meshes directly from the full image without person crops or external 2D cues. To handle this ambiguity, we present UT-HMR ( Uncertainty-guided Temporal HMR), to our knowledge the first one-stage HMR framework to capture correlated pose uncertainty across joints. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-video question answering is challenging since the answer often hinges on a few decisive moments scattered throughout the video, while memory constraints force Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to sample frames at extremely low rates, resulting in sparsity that risks omitting key evidence. Though aggressively enlarging the context size is intuitive, we argue that performance remains fundamentally constrained by the bias, \emph{i.e.}, the misleading cues caused by spurious \textit{linguistic} correlations and salient yet irrelevant \textit{visual} observations. In this paper, we first introduce {S-MME}, a benchmark designed to systematically diagnose shortcut-biased behavior in MLLMs. To mitigate this failure, we further propose a training-free framework, Counterfactual Long-video Evidence-Aware Reasoning (CLEAR). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36269v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Are concepts and mechanisms unified across modalities in current AI models, or instead implemented separately for each one? We operationalize this broad question of modality unification by studying cross-modal steering: 1) finding vectors that successfully steer generation on tokens of one modality, which then 2) transfer zero-shot to steer generation when added to tokens of another modality. Our study goes beyond simple correlational alignment (e.g. representational similarity) because steering is fundamentally causal. We study cross-modal steering in several unified multimodal models (UMMs), since they possess shared parameters for language and image generation, focusing on these two modalities. Across diverse steered concepts such as emotion and object size, we show that steering vectors transfer zero-shot in both directions (text-to-image & image-to-text). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36327v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36337v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) improves model efficiency by sharing representations across related vision tasks, but it often suffers from negative transfer when task updates interfere with one another. Existing conflict-mitigation methods typically operate in gradient space, requiring explicit task-gradient manipulation and additional optimization steps. We propose Conflict-Resolution through Low-Rank Matrices for Multi-Task Learning (CRLoMTL), a parameter-efficient framework that mitigates task interference in the low-rank parameter-update space. CRLoMTL learns task-specific LoRA updates through task-specific passes, where each task updates its own low-rank matrices, and integrates these updates through global shared-subspace fusion. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We tackle the challenge of building real-time interactive video worlds with user-defined behaviors. Such worlds must track object states, apply interaction rules, and render the resulting consequences as users act. Yet existing end-to-end video world models typically learn interaction dynamics within the generator, making it difficult to specify object-level rules and reason about their consequences. Given user-specified rules, a coding agent creates a Box World Engine that determines interaction outcomes and exposes the resulting object states through a lightweight interface of layout boxes, persistent object attributes, and dynamic status variables, leaving appearance and physical effects to generative rendering. Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for breast imaging, but limited labeled data, institutional data fragmentation, and privacy concerns hinder centralized training. We investigate a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with client-level differential privacy. We compare general-purpose CLIP models, biomedical BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 baseline on two public breast imaging datasets, with and without differential privacy. We also evaluate a CLIP ViT-B/16 ablation that removes the text pathway. Evaluation includes patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, baseline comparisons, threshold sensitivity, inter-model agreement, and communication cost. Abstract: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. We introduce SOMA, a benchmark for fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video, comprising 1,632 human-verified questions across three capability axes: body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. Abstract: We present Scalable Pixel-anchored End-to-end Diffusion (SpeeDiff), a latent diffusion method that jointly trains the VAE and the diffusion model from scratch. In principle, joint training allows the diffusion loss gradient to directly guide the VAE encoder, encouraging the formation of a generation-friendly latent space and potentially yielding faster convergence than the conventional two-stage approach with a pretrained frozen VAE. However, a naive end-to-end implementation severely degrades performance, as unrestricted backpropagation of the diffusion loss leads to latent space collapse. Our main technical contribution is a simple yet effective Tweedie Pixel Reconstruction (TPR) loss, which provides additional pixel-level feedback by decoding a predicted clean latent from an intermediate noisy state using Tweedie's formula, thereby alleviating collapse. Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling. articles.content:

Abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has predominantly relied on open-loop imitation learning for training, which presents two limitations. First, expert demonstrations show only one behavior per scenario, so the model cannot learn alternative valid behaviors and, in turn, cannot adapt to user-specified preferences at test time. Second, noise or ambiguity in these demonstrations can produce inconsistent, unreliable supervision for the end-to-end models. Driving is inherently multi-modal: multiple different behaviors can be valid responses to the same scene, and this diversity arises largely from speed rather than path. We introduce a planning paradigm that learns the path through imitation while scoring a set of candidate speeds across multiple criteria with a learned function supervised by physically grounded safety constraints. articles.title: Program-Level Adversarial Co-Adaptive Self-Play for Robotic Security
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36143v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents can adapt robotic software by revising executable programs, but successful responses to an evolving opponent may not remain effective. We present a framework for program-level adversarial co-adaptive self-play in which coding agents generate attacks and defenses from tested opponent code and mission feedback, without model fine-tuning. Environment-specific interfaces support external programs for autonomous driving and SDK-level defenses for humanoid locomotion. Two eight-generation case studies reveal concrete software responses: a driving defender introduces direct-actuation recovery, while a humanoid defender revises incoming-state validation. These responses provide local task recovery but do not establish sustained robustness. The framework makes such adaptation and limitations observable through executable artifacts and task-level evidence.

Abstract: Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. articles.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Navigation vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke costly semantic reasoning even when the next command remains unchanged. Command reuse can reduce computation but risks missing instruction-dependent turns or stops. We introduce ASPEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines temporal observations, language instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence. At eligible command boundaries, sufficient predicted persistence permits command reuse. Otherwise, ASPEN triggers fresh semantic reasoning from the VLA. Evaluated with frozen NaVILA on cross-dataset RxR-CE val-unseen, ASPEN reduces VLA calls by 9.5% and estimated inference time by 8.1%, including scheduling overhead. It maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences

Abstract: Monocular outdoor navigation requires robust camera motion estimation and a dense, navigable map, where 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM serves this task through an explicit differentiable parameterization and closed-form projection. Streaming spatial geometry replaces the per- frame cross-dimensional correspondence with a chunk-level metric prior that supervises tracking and mapping from one source. A ray-conditioned kernel extends each primitive with a viewing-direction subspace that senses the monocular camera viewpoints. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36374v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robotic agents operating in real-world environments must adapt continuously from a stream of multimodal demonstrations, often under constraints that preclude storing or revisiting past data. In this replay-free, single-pass lifelong imitation learning setting, sequential updates can progressively distort the representation space, making expert-based approaches particularly sensitive to routing interference, causing expert selection to degrade over time. We propose HIDRA, a structured routing framework that mitigates this issue through a hierarchical dual-attention mechanism, which decouples instruction-level expert retrieval from context-dependent refinement. To further stabilize routing under representation drift, HIDRA introduces a key-level geometric regularization that enforces both alignment within tasks and separation across tasks. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.36407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. Abstract: A track fitting pipeline is presented that converts a measured racetrack point cloud into a closed, $C^4$ differentiable, three-dimensional surface model suitable for high-fidelity Modelica race-car optimization. Abstract: Drone-based 3D reconstruction and inspection require viewpoints that satisfy image-quality constraints while observing each surface region multiple times, which overlap-based planning heuristics do not guarantee. Abstract: As expansion and scalability in underwater oper- ations becomes more important and challenging, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) become more relevant and the necessity for reliable autonomy more critical. Abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) provide reusable whole-body motion priors: given a kinematic reference, they generate coordinated joint commands for motion replay, teleoperation, and VLA control. However, trained primarily on flat-ground motion, BFMs lack an explicit mechanism to adapt foot placement, swing clearance, and contact timing to local terrain. Many terrain-aware BFM approaches address this limitation by retraining or fine-tuning the tracker together with perception, incurring substantial data and computation costs while coupling ordinary tracking to the perception pathway. Abstract: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Abstract: Differences in musculoskeletal morphology challenge policy reuse across individual models. Here we present MyoAcross, a framework that combines individual musculoskeletal model construction, morphology-conditioned policy learning and virtual model augmentation to enable muscle-driven reference-motion tracking without individual fine-tuning. articles.content:

Abstract: We present CPG-ENN, a trainable quadruped locomotion framework that combines explicit neural coordination with learned motion realization. A single feedback policy modulates six physically interpretable trajectory variables. Abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. articles.title: AI做中学 创未来｜智源SoulAgent持续拓展教育应用
articles.content: 10月19日至24日，北京智源人工智能研究院（以下简称“智源研究院”）连续走进中国人民大学附属中学，先后支持北京市“做中学”领航行动海淀区工作部署会暨科学与工程实践研讨会、“AI做中学，创未来——人工智能赋能创新人才培养研讨会”等活动，围绕SoulAgent在真实课堂、教研和学习场景中的应用开展实践与交流。 SoulAgent是智源研究院推出的“越用越懂你的个人智能体”。在教育场景中，SoulAgent围绕“帮我听课”、教师AI分身、作文批改、教学答疑等方向，探索AI如何帮助教师提升教学效率、沉淀教学内容，同时通过反馈、追问等方式支持学生理解问题、拓展思路、持续思考。 图注：SoulAgent走进校园，围绕真实教学与学习场景开展应用实践。 “帮我听课”：同时听多堂课，让课堂内容持续服务教研公开课、听课和教研等场景中，多门课程往往同时进行，教师既需要关注课堂现场，也要记录内容、梳理重点并完成课后复盘，有限的时间很难兼顾所有感兴趣的课程。SoulAgent“帮我听课”通过AI速记、智能总结和持续问答，辅助记录课堂内容、梳理教学重点。即使无法进入每一间课堂，教师也可以在课后回顾感兴趣的课程，并围绕课堂内容继续提问，让“听课”不再受限于同一时间只能进入一间教室。 10月21日活动期间，27节公开课接入SoulAgent“帮我听课”，通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理等功能，为教师回顾课堂、开展教学复盘提供参考。当天上午多门研究课并行开展，下午随即进入7个教研分论坛，沉淀下来的课堂速记和总结也可以成为后续讨论的共同参考，减少对课堂内容的重复回顾，把更多时间用于教学分析、经验交流和深入研讨。 从课堂记录到课后追问，再到教学复盘和教研交流，SoulAgent希望让一次性的课堂内容进一步沉淀为可查询、可回顾、可持续使用的教学资源。  图注：SoulAgent通过课堂文字整理、教学要点梳理和持续问答，为教师回顾课堂和开展教学复盘提供参考。教师AI分身：让AI先理解教师，再辅助教学如果说“帮我听课”解决的是课堂信息如何被更高效地记录和使用，那么教师AI分身进一步面对的，是AI如何真正适应不同教师的教学方式。 不同教师有自己的课程设计、评价尺度、批注习惯和讲评重点，真实教学并不存在一套完全统一的标准。SoulAgent将教师的课程资料、评价标准、批注样例、讲评口径以及实际使用中的反馈持续沉淀，形成专属教师分身。在此基础上，教师AI分身可以按照具体教师的专业标准，辅助完成作文批改、课堂总结、教学答疑等任务，并在持续使用中逐步贴近教师本人的评价尺度和教学方式。 因此，教师AI分身并不是为所有教师提供同一套“标准答案”，而是将教师自己的知识、经验和专业标准沉淀下来，让AI先理解教师，再按照教师的要求提供辅助。   从教师AI分身到英语作文批改，进入真实教学任务在英语作文批改场景中，教师提供评分标准、批注样例、讲评材料等专业依据，SoulAgent教师AI分身将这些教学标准带入具体批改任务，一个班级的个性化批改报告可以快速生成。 在实际应用中，SoulAgent教师AI分身可以根据具体教学需求，为学生提供更有针对性的修改建议，同时辅助教师梳理班级共性问题、典型案例和改进方向，并将有价值的内容持续沉淀，用于后续讲评、备课和教学。 对学生而言，反馈从一个分数进一步走向具体的问题分析和修改建议；对教师而言，可以减少部分重复性的分析整理工作，把更多时间投入课堂讲评和个别指导；对于教研而言，则可以基于真实教学数据更加系统地发现共性问题和教学重点。 图注：SoulAgent教师AI分身结合教师专业标准，为作文批改、课堂讲评和后续教学提供辅助。 走进校园现场，与一线师生面对面交流两次活动期间，不同学科教师结合课堂记录、备课、作业反馈、教学答疑等实际任务了解和体验SoulAgent，学生也围绕知识问答、课后学习和持续追问等场景进行互动。通过问卷、共创墙和面对面交流，师生分享了对AI辅助教学与学习的实际感受和期待。从帮助教师提升教学效率，到为学生提供更具体的反馈和持续追问支持，AI的价值正在从“更快完成任务”进一步走向“更好支持思考”：让教师把更多专业时间投入教学设计与学生指导，也让学生把更多注意力投入理解、判断和深入思考。  图注：师生围绕SoulAgent教育应用进行现场体验与交流。 未来，智源研究院将继续与中国人民大学附属中学在教育领域深化合作，围绕真实课堂、教研和学习场景持续探索AI教育应用。同时，SoulAgent也将进一步拓展教育、会议智能服务、专家分身等更多应用方向，让“越用越

articles.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
articles.content: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

articles.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

articles.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
articles.content: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. However, existing quantizers eventually saturate as additional codebooks contribute progressively less semantic information. As one approach to alleviating this saturation, we introduce Factorized Vector Quantization, which quantizes complementary, fixed-dimensional views of the visual feature with symmetric parallel codebooks. It continues to improve at larger bit budgets, ultimately matching continuous visual representations in multimodal understanding. Trained on industrial-scale multimodal data, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance among discrete-representation models, outperforming UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2%, respectively, on a nine-metric average. To our knowledge, it is also the first discrete-representation model competitive with strong continuous-representation models such as Qwen3-VL, including on fine-grained OCR tasks. We further identify the key principles and a practical recipe enabling this competitiveness. These results and insights support the potential of discrete visual representations to underpin large-scale native multimodal foundation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/FVQ

articles.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
articles.content: Test-time adaptation helps a deployed model respond to changing inputs, but the same intervention can rescue one batch and damage the next. Updating normalization statistics, for example, can improve corrupted images yet fail when a batch contains mostly one class. Average accuracy hides these failures and cannot tell a model when to use an intervention. Target labels can guide this decision, but they are scarce and some choices are already clear. We introduce PORTAL, a controller that chooses when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying. Each available prediction rule is a candidate, and its predictions are fixed before current feedback arrives. Every acquired label therefore evaluates all candidates on the same input. PORTAL combines these shared comparisons and directs queries toward candidates that can still overtake the current leader. It stops when the remaining labels cannot change the choice or when the possible accuracy gain no longer justifies another query. Our analysis links the required feedback to accuracy gaps and shared mistakes, explaining why some choices need much less evidence. Experiments show that this control turns an intervention that loses accuracy overall into a useful choice on selected batches. It prevents severe failures caused by changes in arrival order and preserves gains across complete corruption streams. When a fixed rule already works well, PORTAL uses little feedback to retain its performance. Periodic label checks reveal when past evidence needs refreshing and help the controller recover as conditions change. The acquired labels also train stronger candidates for future batches, and selection brings nearly all of their accuracy gains into deployment. The same feedback therefore improves both the choice made now and the predictions available to later batches.

articles.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
articles.content: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

articles.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
articles.content: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

articles.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
articles.content: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are commonly distributed in the language of the Kinetic PreProcessor (KPP), which generates efficient Fortran or C code but does not fit into the differentiable programming frameworks in which machine-learning models are developed. We present KPPax, a kinetic preprocessor that generates differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorisable chemistry code in JAX from mechanisms written in the KPP language. KPPax evaluates the rate law with sparse operations in log space, which keeps it differentiable, and integrates the stiff system with the implicit solvers and the forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the \texttt{diffrax} library, so that exact sensitivities are obtained without hand-derived adjoint code. We demonstrate two applications with the POLLU benchmark mechanism. In the first, the Fisher information matrix computed from an automatically differentiated Jacobian predicts, before any fit, which of the 25 rate coefficients a flow-tube-like design can identify, and noisy synthetic estimation confirms the predicted uncertainties of the nine identifiable rate coefficients to within about 30\% while revealing clusters of fast reactions of which only ratios are constrained. In the second, a neural-network correction of an emission inventory is trained offline on per-scenario 4D-Var retrievals and then fine-tuned online through the chemical model, which reduces the error of the biogenic correction by a factor of 2.4--5 and recovers information on low-temperature emissions that the individual retrievals lose. KPPax makes KPP mechanisms directly usable for parameter estimation and hybrid physics--machine-learning modelling.

articles.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
articles.content: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured. We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals. We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum. With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust. On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops. In 13.3 hours of real-robot evaluation over 4,800 unseen goals across 4 objects and diverse wrist orientations, the state-based policy reaches 95.2% of goals within 2 cm and 0.4 rad, and the filter cuts its drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals. The policies can also spin a lightbulb held in an arbitrary pose, reach out-of-distribution goals, withstand fast arm motion and perturbations, and, needing only a wrist camera, serve as portable skills such as screwing in a lightbulb. We release the full recipe as a platform for studying performance, reliability, and safety in high-dimensional dexterous systems. Videos and more are available at https://ian-chuang.github.io/dexsafe/.

articles.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
articles.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

articles.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
articles.content: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
articles.content: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.

articles.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
articles.content: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs.   Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

articles.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
articles.content: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.

articles.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
articles.content: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. We introduce a metacognitive controller that guides diffusion generation according to the needs of the current response and the agent's interaction with the environment. It learns when to finalize tokens and how far generation should extend, reducing overall computation within responses. Our controller, a lightweight plug-in for the diffusion backbone, is trained on agent trajectories to balance correctness and generation cost. This approach connects the agent's generation process to the interaction the agent serves. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that our approach reduces inference FLOPs by 20.6% on average compared with the most efficient baseline, while maintaining competitive task accuracy. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our approach.

articles.title: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence
articles.content: Cross-view object correspondence identifies the same object across views. However, existing methods often rely on frame-wise matching or sequential tracking, which can propagate correspondence errors under appearance changes or occlusions. Therefore, we introduce cross-view temporal object correspondence, which requires preserving object identity across both views and time from a query mask. To address this, we propose XTrack, a unified framework which repurposes a pretrained video DiT with semantic and spatiotemporal priors for RGB-to-mask latent transport, jointly modeling cross-view matching and temporal tracking. However, naive video DiTs do not guarantee accurate cross-view grounding and often attend to semantically similar yet incorrect objects across views. Thus, we introduce focal cross-view attention alignment, hard negative conditioning, and local context crop strategies to ensure reliable grounding. Finally, beyond these architectural enhancements, we also tackle the lack of dense annotation by introducing a pseudo-label curation pipeline that converts sparse Ego-Exo4D annotations into dense supervision to enable effective video-level training. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of XTrack as a unified framework, ensuring robust temporal consistency and identity preservation.

articles.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
articles.content: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. Recent point-in-time models trained on web snapshots from different years provide a way to probe how knowledge prevalence varies over time. Using these models, we propose a temporal variability score (TVS), defined as the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models. A higher score suggests that the knowledge may be less consistently represented across years of web text. We evaluate six benchmarks covering diverse topics using six models from multiple open-source model families. We find that low- and high-TVS items are learned similarly early in training, but high-TVS items improve faster later on. At the end of the pretraining run, high-TVS items outperform low-TVS items in 34 of 36 model-benchmark settings, with an average advantage of 7.3 points of chance-normalized accuracy. This pattern is most robust on knowledge-intensive tasks, even when comparing items of similar difficulty. Our findings reveal differences in how knowledge is learned over the course of pretraining, with temporal variability providing a diagnostic of these learning dynamics beyond aggregate benchmark scores.

articles.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
articles.content: Visual generation requires both high-level semantic knowledge and fine-grained pixel details. We propose a learning paradigm that assigns these roles to autoregressive pretraining for knowledge acquisition and diffusion post-training for high-fidelity rendering. Within this framework, we study the objective, representation, and scaling of knowledge acquisition and rendering. Controlled comparisons identify autoregression as the stronger pretraining objective for downstream rendering, improving both learning efficiency and final generation quality. We further find that AR-only generation quality does not necessarily correlate with final performance; semantic quality matters more. This motivates a purely semantic tokenizer trained with language supervision alone, without an image decoder or reconstruction loss. We establish compute-optimal scaling laws for knowledge acquisition and rendering, and find that autoregressive pretraining lowers the fitted asymptotic rendering loss compared with pixel diffusion models trained from scratch. Guided by the laws, we train a 3B-parameter text-to-image model with only 6,600 H100 GPU-hours, achieving 86 on GenEval and 87 on DPG-Bench and validating the proposed paradigm at scale.

articles.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
articles.content: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates with automatically verified answer keys, in which the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts is crossed while their text is held fixed (480 tasks). Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and two DeepSeek models, both heuristics fail in predictable places. Selecting by relevance readmits decoys, because decoys are on topic: even a perfect relevance filter loses 23 to 31 points to rarest-first selection in the classic hidden-profile configuration. Rarest-first selection is no better than random selection on average and wins only where the rare facts happen to be the useful ones. In both cases accuracy follows the balance of evidence the memory keeps, not the policy that kept it. The decision model adds a third failure, a form of social proof: it gives extra weight to facts attributed to many agents. Removing the attribution tags, or reassigning them at random with line order fixed, raises accuracy in the classic configuration by 13 to 24 points. In natural discussions the evidence is lost before any memory acts: the complete transcript yields lower accuracy than no notes at all.

articles.title: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video
articles.content: Agile robots require spatiotemporal intelligence to interpret scenes, reason about interactions, and anticipate future events. Yet it remains unclear how well foundation vision models support these capabilities, particularly from a moving egocentric camera, which is a natural view for robots. To investigate this, we collect an annotated tennis dataset and train a suite of vision models on spatiotemporal tasks. Our dataset contains egocentric video synchronized with five allocentric videos, estimated global positions, labeled contact times, and annotated stroke types. We then evaluate seven prediction tasks from egocentric images: 2D ego player and 3D ball localization, future player and ball trajectories, forehand or backhand stroke anticipation, time to the next ego player ball contact, and 3D ball position at that contact. We compare image encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models with jointly trained prediction heads. The best performing models achieve mean current-frame localization errors of 0.14 m for the ego player and 0.54 m for the ball, future forecasting errors of 0.34 m for the ego player and 0.91 m for the ball over 1.1 s, and a mean contact-time prediction error of 0.14 s. Auxiliary depth information substantially improves 3D ball localization, suggesting that inferring metric depth remains a challenge. Longer image histories do not improve ball forecasting, indicating that representations exploit scene context rather than rely solely on inter-frame motion. Finally, we propose a conditional diffusion model to generate whole-body kinematic tennis motion from vision encoder predictions on egocentric video at real-time rates, adapting movements as predictions are refined. These results move towards a deeper understanding of how foundation vision models can support real-time dynamic robots using egocentric video.

articles.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
articles.content: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. Existing approaches maintain visual grounding during reasoning in two main ways: they either refer to evidence using textual coordinates, which specify symbolic locations rather than the visual content itself, or reinsert cropped regions or frames into the multimodal context, preserving visual details at the cost of substantial context expansion. To address these limitations, we introduce VideoLVR, which constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, thereby providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps. To supervise latent visual evidence generation, we introduce a visual token prediction objective that formulates visual token reconstruction as prediction over a vocabulary derived from the input video, thereby unifying visual evidence reconstruction and text generation within the same token prediction framework. This shared prediction framework enables MLLMs to reason over interleaved text tokens and latent visual states while integrating evidence from different moments. We further extend VideoLVR to reinforcement learning by treating sampled visual tokens as actions alongside text tokens and jointly optimizing the policy using final-answer rewards. By efficiently revisiting task-relevant visual information during reasoning, VideoLVR improves video understanding without substantially expanding the multimodal context. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness, especially on tasks requiring fine-grained visual evidence.

articles.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive. Under finite rollout budgets, this raises an important question: can data management at the environment level make agentic reinforcement learning (RL) more efficient by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances together with the environments that determine their tools, states, transitions, and verification? To address this question, we introduce EnvSched (Environment-aware Scheduling), an online scheduler that learns from rollout history. EnvSched assigns scheduling value through two complementary modeling choices: exploitation prioritizes tasks likely to provide informative reward differences, while coverage spreads each batch across underobserved environments and interaction patterns. EnvSched organizes environment--task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph, with within-environment edges capturing task semantics and shared tool, state, and verifier structure, and cross-environment edges capturing abstract execution and reward topology. By propagating historical rollout statistics along both edge types, it predicts within-task reward variance. These predictions guide a scheduler that allocates each batch to tasks with high predicted reward variance and underobserved environments and tasks. Environment quotas and a similarity penalty further limit concentration and redundancy, yielding informative and diverse batches without additional pilot rollouts. In RL on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched achieves an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, exceeding the highest score attained by random task selection after 120 steps. It also improves downstream performance across model sizes at the same training budget.

articles.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
articles.content: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. Both use the same interval, level estimate, donor fitting, and crossfade, while the same-class replacement preserves the correct answer. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, different-class replacements produce 49.7 to 60.9 percentage points more answer changes than same-class replacements. Same-class accuracy remains within 5.2 percentage points of original accuracy. Among trials with correct original and same-class answers, soundscape-weighted selective accuracy for the inserted class is 73.7 to 81.9%, averaging eligible trials within each soundscape and then weighting eligible soundscapes equally. This protocol tests how model answers respond to local changes in event class.
